back: Passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task or decide, while the manager remains accountable.
The obligation to report on and justify results to a superior; it cannot be fully delegated.
Authority is the right to decide; responsibility is the duty to complete the task. Authority must match responsibility.
Clear targets, reporting, review meetings, appraisal, audits and consequences for success or failure.
Frees senior time, faster decisions, develops staff, motivates, uses specialist knowledge.
Mistakes, loss of control, training and supervision cost, overload, inconsistency.
With the same staff, wider spans mean fewer managers and levels, and a shorter chain of command.
Over-checking shows distrust and demotivates; no checking risks undetected problems. Balance depends on ability, risk and cost of error.
Skilled staff, clear tasks, limits on authority, regular review, and a culture that accepts learning from mistakes.
